title: Latin Grammy 2024: Nominees List and Female Highlights
seoTitle: Latin Grammy 2024: Nominees & Female Artists Shine
subtitle: The Latin Recording Academy announces the names vying for the 27th Latin Grammy Awards
excerpt: The Latin Recording Academy revealed the nominees for the 27th Latin Grammy Awards. Anitta, Karol G, and Rosalía lead the Album of the Year category and the ceremony.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The Latin Recording Academy has released the full list of nominees for the 27th Latin Grammy Awards, generating significant interest by bringing together names like Anitta, Karol G, and Rosalía in the Album of the Year race. The ceremony is confirmed for November 12th in the United States, which explains the surge in searches on the topic.

Album of the Year Nominees

In the Album of the Year category, the highlights are Anitta with “EQUILIBRIVM”, Karol G with “Tropicoqueta”, and Rosalía with “LUX”. Also competing are Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso – “Free Spirits”, Jorge Drexler – “Tacará”, Silvana Estrada – “Vendrán Suaves Lluvias”, Mon Laferte – “Femme Fatale”, Carín León – “Muda”, Milo J – “La Vida Era Más Corta”, and Rawayana – “¿Dónde es el After?”. The presence of these names reinforces the female power in Latin music.

Best Portuguese Language Song

Among the nominees for Best Portuguese Language Song are Urias with “Águas de um Mar Azul”, Criolo, Amaro de Freitas, and Dino D'Santiago with “No Vento de Nós”, Marisa Monte with “Sua Onda”, Johnny Hooker and Ney Matogrosso with “Viver e Morrer de Amor na América Latina”, and also the collaboration between Rosalía and Carminho – “Memórias”.

Brazilian Best New Artist

Representing Brazil in the Best New Artist category, Zeca Veloso joins the list alongside other names, still being updated, such as Delilah Fabian, Loulu Gilberto, Arath Herce, Macario Martínez, Maye Sofia, Monroy Kendall, Peña Dora, Sanches Aria, and Vega.

Date, Location, and Other Categories

The awards ceremony will take place on November 12th in the United States, bringing together artists who perform in Spanish and Portuguese. In addition to the categories mentioned, the list includes nominations for Record of the Year, such as Ca7riel and Paco Amoroso – “Ha Ha”, Jorge Drexler – “¿Cómo Se Ama?”, and Silvana Estrada – “Dime”.

Other List Highlights

Other names featured in the nominations include Juanes and Vivir Quintana with “Humano”, Rosalía, Yahritza y su Esencia with “La Perla”, Santana and Becky G with “Mi Gran Amor”, and Milo J with “Niño”. The variety of styles and collaborations highlights the diversity of contemporary Latin music.

With information from POPLine.
